name: Clafoutis
description: A Limousin batter pudding of cherries baked in a thick eggy custard until puffed golden like a sweet Dutch baby.
ingredients: a handful of fresh chervil, chopped
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with extra-virgin olive oil.
In a large bowl, whisk together the brioche and cracked black peppercorns until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the Dijon mustard with the dry white wine until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 35 mins.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
tips: Bring your Dijon mustard to room temperature before mixing for a smoother, more even texture.
This keeps well for a couple of days in an airtight container, and the flavor often improves overnight.
